bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Database-led search model: India's recruitment market is structurally different from job-posting-led developed markets, and Naukri's leadership for over 20 years rests on recruiters proactively searching a resume database rather than only reviewing inbound applications
- Scale of the jobseeker database - the MD & CEO's message (routed to the sibling strategy_outlook bundle) states approximately 118 Million resumes with around 25,000 new profiles added daily for the quarter ending June 30, 2026
- Platform flywheel and network effects: every additional recruiter, candidate and interaction improves matching quality and the value delivered to all participants, compounding into an advantage the AR states is increasingly difficult for competitors to replicate
- Distribution: one of the industry's largest direct sales and customer engagement organisations, with a presence across more than 75 cities and deep relationships with enterprises, recruitment consultants, GCCs, start-ups and SMBs
- Two decades of trusted brands, large user ecosystems and proprietary datasets generated through billions of platform interactions - stated to be difficult to replicate and more valuable in an AI-driven world
- Recruitment is the largest and most profitable business and has provided the financial strength to fund technology, new businesses and one of India's leading internet investment portfolios
- Diversified portfolio across four verticals at different maturity stages, each holding a stated market leadership position
- Strong liquidity position - the Company states it holds sufficient cash and cash equivalents to safeguard core operations from financial risk, and channels a part into financial investments
- Investment platform track record: direct early-stage investing has already delivered the listings of Eternal and PB Fintech; AIF schemes give exposure to a stated 135 startups concentrated in AI, deeptech and consumer tech
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Concentration in recruitment — The Company states it relies heavily on the recruitment business in India for its profits and cash flows. Mitigation cited is that recruitment revenues are spread across several industry segments and that Info Edge has been consciously diversifying into other businesses to de-risk the dependency - the AR quantifies the progress as 'The Company's other businesses now contribute 26.1% of the total standalone revenue', i.e. recruitment still accounts for roughly three-quarters. A second concentration is geographic: the BRSR states overseas revenue is only 6.43% of total revenue, so the portfolio is almost entirely exposed to the Indian cycle.
- AI disintermediation of search-led discovery, and failure to transform existing services with AI — Two-sided technology risk stated explicitly. Externally, AI chatbots and AI-generated search summaries let users get answers without visiting content platforms - management calls the resulting decline in organic traffic the single most important development for Shiksha in FY26 and says the challenge is particularly acute for guidance platforms that monetise attention rather than transactions. Internally, the AR states that if Info Edge is unable to transform existing services by leveraging AI, or if its AI and big data capabilities fail to yield satisfactory results, its platforms may not effectively match users, recommend services or scale new AI-first offerings, potentially affecting win rates, market share, revenue and profits; more broadly innovation could render existing propositions redundant.
- Data security and privacy — The Company stores and processes large volumes of personal and behavioural data and faces technical failures, server breakdowns, data corruption, security breaches and improper use or disclosure of personal information; any such event could deter users, damage reputation, create legal liability, invite regulatory scrutiny and materially affect the business. The BRSR names Cybersecurity and Data Privacy as material issue #1 and specifies regulatory penalties under India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 as a negative financial implication. Mitigations stated: a secondary disaster recovery site in India, continuous AI/ML-driven security monitoring, data encryption, network protection, internal and third-party assessment, industry-standards compliance and proactive management of technology obsolescence.
- Investment portfolio risk (startup and AIF exposure) — The AR states the Company carries a large exposure to investee startups spanning listed, non-listed and strategic investments, that these may not generate returns and could absorb additional cash during incubation or early stages, and that a substantial part of investments made over the years has already been written off, exited or provisioned for - described as calculated risks forming part of the growth strategy. Critically, it also warns that reported equity holdings in investee companies may not translate into an equivalent economic interest, due to the terms of investment (including senior rights granted to certain investors) or ESOP-related dilution. Exposure and write-off amounts are financial-statement data and are deliberately not extracted here.
- Competition across every vertical — All of the Company's platforms face direct competition in both online and offline spaces. Managed through continuous competitive tracking, product innovation, brand investment and customer engagement. This sits alongside 'Brand Value' risk - the platforms are built on well-known brands, and any negative implication for those brands, amplified by the reach of social media, is called a significant risk.
- Network effects, platform integrity and user-generated content liability — Most of the portfolio depends on network effects - platform value rises with user count - so declining participation, quality erosion or platform disintermediation is a direct business risk. Separately, users may engage in intentional or negligent misconduct including fraudulent postings, spam or inappropriate content, which may damage brand image or expose the Company to claims such as defamation or invasion of privacy; continuous web-traffic monitoring, content filters and profile verification are the stated controls.
- Evolving regulatory and privacy environment — The Company operates where government continues to consider regulation of various facets of online businesses, with many such regulations at different levels of deliberation that could significantly impact product offerings and services. Changes in privacy laws may impact its ability to collect, process or share personal data; it typically seeks users' prior consent before sharing, but the evolving legal landscape requires continuing attention (the sentence is truncated in the source).
- Macroeconomic, geopolitical and treasury exposure — Revenues from certain segments are sensitive to the economic cycle, with trade wars, tariff barriers, geopolitical conflict, persistent inflation and tighter financial conditions named; business diversification and a healthy balance sheet are the stated mitigants. Related treasury risk: the Company holds significant cash and cash equivalents to preserve financial flexibility, and channels part of it into treasury investments to earn returns, exposing it to market conditions and interest-rate movements - managed through prudent balance-sheet management and a defined investment framework. A third channel is capital availability: given the current phase of the expansion strategy, the Company may need additional capital and could face challenges obtaining it in a timely manner or on acceptable terms.
- Human capital, attrition and workforce risk — BRSR material issue #2 (Human Capital Development) cites the high turnover rate in the internet software and services sector and the need to manage the talent pool, foster engagement and ensure retention, with high cost of talent acquisition and training named as a negative financial implication. The scale of this is disclosed in BRSR item 22 (routed to the sibling registry/profile/governance bundles rather than this one): the permanent-employee turnover rate was 30.00% in FY26, 30.00% in FY25 and 26.19% in FY24 - i.e. structurally elevated and rising versus FY24 - against a permanent headcount of 5,878 (6,268 including non-permanent). The Directors' Report states attrition remained controlled despite elevated market demand in specialised areas such as AI and UX.
- Strategic acquisition, integration and intellectual-property risk — Focused investments through strategic partners carry the risk of acquiring a business that does not align with core offerings, values or principles, and the Company also assumes potential liabilities arising from past-period regulatory non-compliance by acquired businesses; existing or future alliances, long-term investments and acquisitions may materially affect business, reputation and results. Separately, the Company may be unable to adequately protect its intellectual property; third-party infringement of its trademarks is possible and litigation is time- and resource-intensive and may be ongoing, and its businesses rely on specific registered domains whose continued ownership and renewal carry risk.

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Business structure slide splits the company into "OPERATING BUSINESSES" and "INVESTMENTS", describing Recruitment as "India's largest online job classifieds ecosystem" and Real Estate as "A leading platform in online real estate classifieds"; Matchmaking is "Connecting millions for meaningful relationships" and Education "Guiding students toward smarter education & career" (slide text truncated mid-sentence).
- The Company is "primarily engaged in the business of internet based service delivery operating in four service verticals through various web portals": recruitment solutions (primarily naukri.com plus other recruitment portals and ancillary services), 99acres.com, Jeevansathi.com and Shiksha.com.
- Only "Recruitment Solutions" and "99acres" are reportable segments; "the 'Other segments' comprises primarily Jeevansathi & Shiksha verticals are not considered as reportable operating segment since they individually do not meet qualifying criteria for the reportable segment as per Ind AS 108".
- MD & CEO Hitesh Oberoi states "99acres continued to strengthen its market leadership and moved closer to breakeven, while Jeevansathi remained profitable during the quarter."
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Group merger] Scheme of Amalgamation approved Aug 09, 2024 to merge wholly owned subsidiaries Axilly Labs, Diphda Internet Services, Zwayam Digital and (added Feb 05, 2025) Allcheckdeals India into Info Edge; NCLT's April 07, 2026 order was appealed, NCLAT subsequently passed a favourable order dispensing with the Transferee Company's meetings, and the second motion petition has been filed before NCLT New Delhi for sanction of the Scheme.
- [JV exit - Shopkirana] Entire shareholding in Shopkirana E-Trading, held via Startup Investments (Holding) Limited (SIHL), was transferred to Trustroot Internet Private Limited (brand 'Udaan') during the quarter; consideration was 104,868 preference shares of TIPL "aggregating to 2.021% on fully converted and diluted basis at a value of USD 314.40 per share (aggregating to about USD 32.97 Million)", with SIHL separately investing USD 1.72 million for 5,484 preference shares. Shopkirana ceased to be a joint venture.
- [JV swap - Gramophone/Unnati] Entire shareholding in Agstack Technologies ('Gramophone') was transferred to Akshamaala Solutions ('Unnati') for 49,145 preference shares (15.75% of Unnati fully diluted), plus Rs 350.00 million primary infusion for 18,756 preference shares, "thereby taking the aggregate shareholding of SIHL in Unnati to 20.25%"; Gramophone ceased to be a JV and Unnati became a JV.
- [Portfolio IPO] SIHL's board on November 6, 2025 approved "a proposed partial divestment in NoPaperForms Solutions Limited... as a part of its proposed Initial Public Offering (IPO) process including pre-IPO secondary transaction(s)", subject to regulatory clearances.
- [Listed investments] Gains/losses on Eternal Limited (formerly Zomato Limited) and PB Fintech Limited are fair-valued through OCI; following NCLT approval dated August 29, 2025, JV Makesense Technologies merged into PB Fintech and the PB Fintech shares received were reclassified as a financial investment fair valued at each reporting date under Ind AS 109.
- [Regulation] "On November 21, 2025, the Government of India notified the four 'Labour Codes'... consolidating 29 existing labour laws", introducing a uniform definition of wages and enhanced leave and gratuity provisions; the remeasurement impact has been disclosed under exceptional items.
business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: Info Edge operates web portals, online classified media and allied services - stated in the BRSR as 100% of turnover under a single main activity ('Data Processing, hosting and related activities; web portals', NIC code 63122). The Company runs four operating verticals: Recruitment led by Naukri (serving enterprises, GCCs and recruitment consultants on one side and jobseekers on the other, across enterprise hiring solutions, specialised recruitment platforms, AI-powered recruitment products, talent sourcing automation, jobseeker services and skill assessment, complemented by Job Hai in the value segment), Real Estate through 99acres (brokers, builders and owners), Matchmaking through Jeevansathi and Aisle (prospective matches, brides and grooms), and Education through Shiksha (students, colleges and universities). Strategically the business is described as two portfolios - the operating businesses and financial investments - the latter deployed both directly from the balance sheet and through wholly-owned subsidiaries, and through Alternate Investment Fund schemes managed by Info Edge Ventures.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Recruitment:** Naukri (flagship recruitment platform), Job Hai (value / blue- and grey-collar segment), NaukriGulf (Middle East hiring platform), iimjobs (premium / leadership hiring), Hirist (specialised technology hiring), Naukri Top Tier, PremiumX, Talent Pulse (AI-powered talent intelligence platform), AI-Rex (agentic AI-powered recruitment talent sourcing platform), Zwayam (recruitment workflow software; strategic investment, 100%), DoSelect / Axilly Labs (skill assessment solutions; strategic investment, 100%)
- **Recruitment - jobseeker services (back-filled from the MD & CEO's message / MD&A routed to the sibling strategy_outlook bundle):** Naukri 360 (self-serve, online-first jobseeker suite), Neo (jobseeker agent), AI Resume Maker, AI Mock Interview Prep, Naukri FastForward, Naukri Minis
- **Real Estate:** 99acres, 99Shorts (Instagram-style short-video feed for real-estate project discovery, launched in NCR; stated in the MD & CEO's message routed to the sibling capex_expansion/strategy_outlook bundles)
- **Matchmaking:** Jeevansathi, Aisle (serious-intent dating; wholly owned), Arike (Malayalam), Anbe (Tamil), Neetho (Telugu), Neene (Kannada) - regional dating apps under Aisle (stated in the Directors' Report routed to the sibling strategy_outlook bundle)
- **Education:** Shiksha (higher-education guidance, domestic and study-abroad)
- **Financial investments:** Direct investments from the balance sheet and through wholly-owned subsidiaries, AIF schemes managed by Info Edge Ventures: IE Venture Fund I (including follow-on), IE Venture Investment Fund II, Capital 2B Fund I, IE Venture Investment Fund III, B8 Fund I, A88 Fund I

outlook.body:
- Naukri's long-term strategy is anchored on five complementary growth pillars, centred on expanding leadership across India's recruitment ecosystem and growing not only with hiring volumes but by expanding its share of recruitment spending, increasing monetisation across the customer base and broadening participation across the end-to-end hiring lifecycle.
- Pillar - strengthen leadership in the core mid-market recruitment franchise (compensation levels of approximately Rs 5-30 Lakh, described as the largest component of India's organised white-collar recruitment market) by expanding customer acquisition, increasing SME penetration, strengthening presence across Tier II and Tier III cities and raising recruiter productivity through AI-powered search, matching and talent sourcing automation.
- Pillar - increase revenue per recruiter through value-added offerings: recruitment intelligence, employer branding, recruitment marketing, talent sourcing automation and assisted hiring solutions.
- Pillar - expand premium hiring through a multi-brand ecosystem (Naukri, iimjobs, Hirist, PremiumX, Naukri TopTier) addressing leadership, management and specialised technology hiring, monetised via higher-value recruiter subscriptions, premium talent access, employer branding and AI-enabled recruitment services.
- Pillar - scale the value segment (blue- and grey-collar): strengthen Job Hai's leadership in markets where it already has traction, then gradually expand into additional metropolitan and large urban centres.
- Pillar - deepen jobseeker engagement and monetisation beyond job discovery, through the Naukri 360 / Naukri FastForward / Naukri Minis / Neo ecosystem covering resume enhancement, interview preparation, personalised job discovery, career guidance and curated content, with jobseeker engagement expected to become an increasingly important driver of user lifetime value, platform stickiness and long-term revenue diversification.
- Turn Naukri's AI and data capabilities into standalone enterprise revenue streams (Talent Pulse for talent intelligence, executive intelligence, AI-Rex for agentic talent sourcing), expanding the addressable market from hiring into talent intelligence and strategic workforce planning and repositioning Naukri from a hiring platform to a broader talent solutions partner.
- Shift Naukri's jobseeker business to a self-serve, online-first model via Naukri 360 - described as a defining strategic move.
- 99acres: convert established traffic leadership into supply, response and revenue leadership across key markets, with the intense investment phase stated to be behind it and operating leverage expected to play out; residential resale (its strongest segment) is the network-effects core and new homes is the early-stage expansion.
- 99acres: make early inroads into the new-projects/new-homes advertising market historically dominated by Meta and Google for developer advertising spend, including the 99Shorts short-video discovery feed launched in NCR with expansion to other major cities planned.
- Matchmaking: Jeevansathi to solidify its dominant position in Hindi-speaking markets while optimising marketing efficiency; Aisle to focus on product-led improvements and deeper regional matchmaking; the stated focus is to sustain high revenue growth while keeping the combined portfolio at or near breakeven and contributing to long-term cash generation. Recommendations, matching and pricing at Jeevansathi are now fully AI-driven.
- Job Hai: build for blue-collar hiring what Naukri built for white-collar - a trusted, data-rich, high-frequency platform that becomes the default for both employers and jobseekers - monetised across job postings, database access, job boost, assisted hiring and WhatsApp-based outreach, serving SMBs, enterprise clients and recruitment consultants.
- Shiksha: complete the pivot from education-related content discovery / information provision to a comprehensive counselling and marketing services proposition, capitalise on the sustained expansion of private universities and colleges in India, and diversify study abroad towards emerging destinations - while maintaining a focus on capital efficiency and improved cash generation.
- NaukriGulf: continue the evolution from an Indian professional diaspora platform into a regional Middle East hiring platform serving a diverse employer base across multiple industries and geographies.
- Group: continue to support innovation through investments in technology-led businesses and alternative investment funds, while maintaining a disciplined approach to capital allocation and risk management, backed by a strong balance sheet.
- Group: embed AI across all businesses and launch AI-native products, on the stated conviction that proprietary data, domain expertise and customer relationships become more valuable in an AI-driven world.
- Stated philosophy: the Board is described as trustee of investors' capital, responsible for maximising shareholder value over the long term. The Company states a consistent and 'impressive' track record of dividend payments in line with its approved Dividend Distribution Policy, which was REVISED during FY26 to align with the amended Listing Regulations - the revision expanded the factors and circumstances considered for declaring dividend, provided additional avenues for utilisation of retained earnings, and revised the target dividend payout framework (policy published at www.infoedge.in/pdfs/Dividend-Policy.pdf). During FY26 the Company paid a final dividend for FY25 of Rs 3.60 per share (180% of the Rs 2 face value; declared August 25, 2025, record date July 25, 2025 - normal sequencing for a final dividend approved at an AGM) and two interim dividends for FY26 of Rs 2.40 per share each (120%), declared November 12, 2025 (record November 21, 2025) and February 13, 2026 (record February 20, 2026); the Board on May 22, 2026 recommended a further final dividend of Rs 3.60 per share for FY26, subject to shareholder approval at the 31st AGM on Tuesday, August 25, 2026, with record date Friday July 24, 2026 and payment on or after Wednesday September 2, 2026 (payout amounts deliberately not extracted). The Company does not propose to transfer any amount to reserves. Capital structure: the members approved a sub-division/split of equity by postal ballot on April 11, 2025 (the sentence describing the split ratio is truncated in the source; the face value is stated elsewhere as Rs 2 per share and paid-up capital as Rs 1,296.84 Million in the BRSR). Investment philosophy: the Company maintains a strong liquidity position, holding sufficient cash and cash equivalents to safeguard core operations from financial risk, and channels part of that cash into financial investments through a hybrid approach - direct investments from the balance sheet and through wholly-owned subsidiaries into early-stage startups, plus structured investments through six AIF schemes managed by Info Edge Ventures - while stating it will continue to support innovation through these investments 'while maintaining a disciplined approach towards capital allocation and risk management'. Governance of shareholder money: 1,985 equity shares were transferred to the IEPF Authority during FY26 along with Rs 3,84,700 of unclaimed dividends (FY25 final plus both FY26 interims); the Remuneration Policy was amended by the Board on May 22, 2026 to revise the commission payable to Independent Directors with effect from April 1, 2026; a Whistle Blower mechanism with an Independent External Ombudsman (M/s Thought Arbitrage Consulting) received 2 complaints in FY26, all investigated and resolved, and no Director or employee was denied access to the Audit Committee Chairperson.
- Materiality: the BRSR identifies exactly six material responsible business conduct issues, five of them classified 'Opportunity & Risk' and one 'Opportunity' - (1) Governance: Cybersecurity and Data Privacy, (2) Social: Human Capital Development, (3) Social: Customer satisfaction, (4) Social: Community Development (opportunity only), (5) Environmental: Energy Management and clean technology implementation, (6) ESG: Supply Chain Sustainability. No financial implication is quantified anywhere in that table - the 'financial implications' column is qualitative throughout - and the mitigation column is a stated nil dash ('-') for issues 3 and 4.
- Clean energy: the Company states the successful installation and commissioning of a 250 kW rooftop solar power plant as the exemplar of its clean-tech investment.
- Energy management: reduction and optimal utilisation of energy through an automated energy monitoring solution named 'Zenatix', energy-efficient illumination fixtures, power factor rationalisation and addition of VFDs in the HVAC system. Data centre operations and office facilities are acknowledged as energy-intensive.
- Certifications and standards mapped in BRSR Section B item 4: ISO 45001:2018 against Principles P2, P3, P4, P5, P7 and P8; ISO 27001:2022 Information Security Management System against P9; certain portions of the business (based on applicability) compliant with Payment Card Industry Data Security Standards and assessed annually; SOC 2 Type 2 Security Compliance certification for subsidiaries Naukri and Zwayam; PCI-DSS compliance for subsidiaries Naukri and Jeevansathi. Principles P1 and P6 carry a stated nil dash - NO standard or certification is mapped to the integrity principle or to the environment principle.
- Policy architecture: all nine NGRBC principles are covered by policies, all Board-approved, all translated into procedures, and all extended to value-chain partners (Yes across P1-P9). Named policies include the Whistleblower Policy, Code of Ethics & Conduct, Anti-Bribery and Anti-Corruption (ABAC) Policy, Code of Conduct to Regulate, Monitor and Report Trading by Insiders, Fair Disclosure Code, Gift Policy, Policy for Redressal of Investor Grievances, ESG Policy, Policy for Personal Investments and Engagement by Executive Leadership with Other Entities, Sustainable Supply Chain Policy, Supplier Code of Conduct, IT Security Policy, Health and Safety Policy, HR Policy, Human Rights Policy, POSH Code of Conduct, Workforce Redressal Guidelines, CSR Policy, Procurement Policy and the Dividend Distribution Policy.
- Supply chain: a Sustainable Supply Chain Policy and Supplier Code of Conduct apply to value-chain partners, with due diligence at partner selection, expectations set out in contracts and comprehensive documentation; anti-corruption, anti-bribery and confidentiality clauses are written into vendor and contractor contracts. Stated absence worth noting: 'no formal training was provided to value chain partners during the current financial year' - partners only have access to the policy.
- Ethics record (stated nils): Nil Directors, Nil KMPs and Nil employees had disciplinary action taken against them by any law enforcement agency for bribery or corruption in FY26 and FY25 (Workers 'NA' - not applicable, since the Company classifies its entire workforce as Employees and no personnel as Workers); Nil complaints in relation to conflict of interest of Directors or of KMPs in FY26 and FY25; and 'Not applicable, as there have been no instances of corruption and conflicts of interest against the Company in the FY26' for corrective action. Note the '-' entries in the Remarks columns are stated nils, not missing data.
- Whistle-blower and grievance: an Independent External Ombudsman (M/s Thought Arbitrage Consulting) operates the vigil mechanism; 2 whistle-blower complaints were received in FY26, duly investigated and resolved, and no Director or employee was denied access to the Chairperson of the Audit Committee. The BRSR fragment also records that the 2 complaints pending at the close of FY25 were resolved subsequent to that year-end.
- POSH (back-filled with provenance from the Directors' Report routed to the sibling capex_expansion bundle, not present in this risks_esg bundle): 4 complaints were received in FY26 under the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act, all disposed of within statutory timelines, none pending beyond ninety days and none pending as at March 31, 2026; the Internal Complaints Committee includes an external member and a majority of women members. The Company is also stated to be compliant with the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961.
- Assurance and boundary: the BRSR is prepared on a STANDALONE basis (entity only, not the consolidated group) and has obtained Reasonable Assurance from SGS India Private Limited - a stronger assurance level than the limited assurance that is common - which matters because the group's consolidated footprint (15 subsidiaries plus associates and six AIF schemes) sits outside the assured boundary.
- Employee profile disclosed in BRSR item 20 (relevant to the social pillar): 5,878 permanent employees (62.90% male / 37.10% female) plus 390 other-than-permanent (interns, freelancers, retainers and third-party contractors), total 6,268 (61.89% / 38.11%); 87 employees with disabilities, identified only from income-tax self-disability declarations because the Company states it is an equal opportunity employer and does not specifically track disabled employees. The 'Other than Permanent' differently-abled row is a stated nil dash ('-'), i.e. zero, not unknown. No personnel are classified as 'Workers' anywhere in the report.
- TRUNCATION DEFECT - ESG targets not readable: the BRSR block ends mid-question at '5. Specific commitments, goals and targe[ts]', which is precisely the disclosure that would have carried the Company's stated ESG commitments, goals and targets with defined timelines. No quantified ESG target (emissions, energy, water, diversity, renewable share) can therefore be reported from the routed text; their absence here is a gap in the extract, NOT evidence that the Company set none.

outlook.body: Info Edge is an asset-light internet-platform business and has no physical capacity programme: BRSR Section A item 18 states 'Not Applicable' against Number of plants for both National and International rows (it does not state zero or a nil dash), against 113 offices in India and 7 offices internationally. Expansion is therefore stated as platform, product, geographic-footprint and capability build-out rather than plant or capacity addition. Product/geographic expansion named in the year: 99Shorts, an Instagram-style short-video feed for real-estate project discovery, was recently launched in NCR with expansion to other major cities planned in the coming year, as 99acres attacks the new-projects advertising market historically dominated by Meta and Google; Job Hai, already market leader in Delhi NCR, is building the playbook for expansion into Mumbai, Bengaluru and other key metros, with the stated immediate priority being to strengthen leadership where traction exists before gradually expanding into additional metropolitan and large urban centres; Shiksha is pivoting from information provision to a comprehensive counselling and marketing services proposition and diversifying study abroad towards emerging destinations. Capability build-out: during the year several restructuring interventions were undertaken, particularly across the Recruitment business, with Naukri undergoing strategic restructuring to enable sharper ownership and stronger category focus, product organisations augmented with AI-first roles and leadership structures strengthened across iimjobs and allied verticals; hiring was calibrated and focused on Product, Sales, Leadership and Digital functions with a significant push toward AI-native talent to accelerate an 'AI-first transformation'; leadership programmes Catalyst, iLead and Momentum and AI capability programmes AI Accelerate, AIverse and Build Your Own Agent (BYOA) workshops were run. Investment-platform expansion: capital is deployed both directly from the balance sheet and through wholly-owned subsidiaries, and through six AIF schemes managed by Info Edge Ventures - IE Venture Fund I (including follow-on), IE Venture Investment Fund II, Capital 2B Fund I, IE Venture Investment Fund III, B8 Fund I and A88 Fund I - in which Info Edge's stated effective holdings as of March 31, 2026 are c. 50%, 44.7% and 45.2% in Fund I, Fund II and Capital 2B respectively, c. 89% in IE Venture Investment Fund III and 100% in each of B8 Fund I and A88 Fund I; collectively these funds are stated to give exposure to a diversified portfolio of 135 startups concentrated in AI, deeptech and consumer tech, alongside SaaS, fintech and B2B e-commerce (the scheme corpus column is a rupee table and is deliberately not reproduced here). The one named-disclosure figure supplied with this bundle is a fund-raising, not a capital-expenditure, number: 'As of March 2026, IEVI Fund III had received capital commitments of [Rs] 7,903 Million from internal and external investors' - the following sentence, 'IEVI Fund III is also expected to receive further', is TRUNCATED mid-sentence in the source, so the size and timing of the expected further commitments cannot be read and is not stated here. On the rupee quantum of actual capex, the AR's own capital-commitments note is present in the bundle only as a stub - the line 'Capital expenditure contracted for at the end of the year but not recognised as liabilities is as follows: (Rs Mn)' appears with NO figure beneath it, and the page-171 fragment carries only a cross-reference ('Note: For pending capital commitment in respect of related parties kindly refer note 21(b).'), so the contracted-capex amount is UNKNOWN from this text rather than nil. Separately, BRSR Principle 2 Essential Indicator 1 (percentage of R&D and capex investments in technologies improving environmental and social impacts) prints '-' (stated nil) on the R&D row for both the current and previous FY, while the Capex row is printed with NO value at all in either year - a genuine blank, i.e. unknown, and the two must not be collapsed; the accompanying note states only that, given the nature of its services, the Company has directed R&D and capital expenditure towards improving Information Technology efficiencies and has over previous years made substantial investments in upgrading IT infrastructure including software, communication networks and equipment.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Gross hiring demand, not net employment creation, is the driver for recruitment platforms: elevated attrition plus reduced bench strength increases reliance on external hiring, and management states that as companies replace attrition and step up growth investments it expects hiring activity to strengthen further.
- Hiring activity in FY26 remained measured, with IT services subdued for much of the year while several non-IT sectors (hospitality, healthcare, retail, education, real estate) were more resilient; the Naukri JobSpeak Index stabilised in the latter part of the year after two years of moderation.
- GCC expansion is a structural demand driver - India hosts more than 2,100 GCCs, which continue to expand hiring across engineering, product development, AI, cybersecurity and digital transformation; within GCCs, smaller and mid-sized centres continued to hire actively while larger GCCs moved more deliberately.
- Demand for AI, data science, cybersecurity and product-engineering professionals continues to grow significantly faster than the broader market, driving the rapid growth of premium hiring where the Company states it is gaining market share.
- Geographic broadening of hiring into Tier II and Tier III cities creates new employment clusters and expands the addressable market.
- Formalisation of blue- and grey-collar employment, urbanisation and growth in logistics, manufacturing, retail, healthcare, hospitality and platform-based employment expand long-term demand for organised value-segment hiring (Job Hai).
- AI is framed as both opportunity and threat: it is accelerating the industry's transition to intelligent, automated, data-driven hiring rather than replacing recruitment platforms, but AI chatbots and AI-generated search summaries are compressing organic traffic for content-led education platforms.
- Real estate demand: the Indian residential market sustained its post-pandemic upcycle through CY25, supported by a cumulative 125 basis point repo-rate reduction since February 2025, with buyer interest gravitating to higher-value homes; entering CY26 the market has moved into a more measured consolidation phase as price appreciation tests entry-level affordability, though long-term demand drivers are stated to remain intact.
- Real estate structural drivers cited: urban population projected to reach 600 Million by 2030, cumulative affordable-housing demand estimated at 31.2 Million units, premiumisation, a renewed development cycle with regional diversification, and digital transformation of property discovery with active internet users exceeding one billion.
- Digital platforms in India act primarily as discovery and lead-generation channels with transactions closing offline, so platform value is measured through responses and enquiries rather than completed transactions - a highly fragmented market with millions of independent brokers and no single controlling intermediary.
- Commercial office demand: India's office market closed 2025 at a record 86.4 Million Sq. Ft. of transactions (20% YoY growth), with GCCs the largest occupier segment at ~32.6 Million Sq. Ft. (38% of absorption) and Q1 CY26 setting a new quarterly high of 29.9 Million Sq. Ft.
- Education demand: over 1.8 Million Indian students study abroad, but US student-visa issuances to Indian nationals are contracting sharply (peak-season issuances down nearly 70% YoY), Canadian enrolments fell 41% (233,532 in 2023 to 137,608 in 2024) and UK study visas fell 26% before recovering to 95,231 in 2025 - management expects Shiksha revenue to decline in the near term as a result, combined with AI-driven traffic compression.
- Domestic education demand is supported by the sustained expansion of private universities and colleges offering a wider range of courses - explicitly called a widening opportunity for Shiksha's footprint and counselling capability.
- Macro backdrop: the IMF projects global GDP growth of 3.0% in CY26 and 3.4% in CY27 against 3.5% in CY25, and India's real GDP growth at 6.4% in FY26 and 6.7% in FY27; three channels are named through which global conditions reach Info Edge - export-oriented (IT services) hiring demand, overseas education/visa policy, and global capital flows affecting technology valuations and the investment portfolio.
- NaukriGulf benefited from healthy Middle East hiring for most of the year with moderation towards the end owing to regional conflicts.
- Investment portfolio: major listed investees including Eternal Limited and PB Fintech Limited are stated to have scaled their businesses and improved profitability, creating long-term shareholder value (no investee financials or fair values extracted).
- No order book or contracted-pipeline disclosure exists - Info Edge is a subscription/classifieds internet platform, not an order-driven business, and none of the routed text mentions an order book, order inflow or pipeline in that sense.
- The nearest disclosed supply/pipeline analogues (which are platform inventory, NOT an order book and NOT contracted revenue): 99acres had over 1.3 Million total listings with daily fresh supply in residential resale up more than 40% over the past two years and supply share crossing 50%; Job Hai had 130,000+ live jobs across 640+ cities and 45+ job categories.

Management explicitly flags that the single most important development for Shiksha during FY26 was a visible decline in organic traffic, as AI chatbots and AI-generated search summaries let users get answers without visiting content platforms - a risk it calls particularly acute for guidance platforms that monetise attention rather than transactions.
99acres has a near-term goal of 60% web traffic time share (from 51% in March 2026, up from 32% in June 2024).

Management expects revenue in the education business (Shiksha) to decline in the near term, owing to AI-compressed organic traffic and a study-abroad segment hit by immigration negativity and tightening visa policies.

Job Hai, already the market leader in Delhi NCR, is building the playbook for expansion into Mumbai, Bengaluru and other key metros, with the immediate priority being to strengthen leadership where traction is established before gradually widening to additional metropolitan and large urban centres.
Management expects Job Hai to be a significant contributor to group revenue in the medium to long term.

The matchmaking portfolio is to sustain high revenue growth while maintaining a disciplined investment approach that keeps the portfolio at or near breakeven and contributes to long-term cash flow generation (Directors' Report).

risks.note: The Company states it relies heavily on the recruitment business in India for its profits and cash flows. Mitigation cited is that recruitment revenues are spread across several industry segments and that Info Edge has been consciously diversifying into other businesses to de-risk the dependency - the AR quantifies the progress as 'The Company's other businesses now contribute 26.1% of the total standalone revenue', i.e. recruitment still accounts for roughly three-quarters. A second concentration is geographic: the BRSR states overseas revenue is only 6.43% of total revenue, so the portfolio is almost entirely exposed to the Indian cycle.

Two-sided technology risk stated explicitly. Externally, AI chatbots and AI-generated search summaries let users get answers without visiting content platforms - management calls the resulting decline in organic traffic the single most important development for Shiksha in FY26 and says the challenge is particularly acute for guidance platforms that monetise attention rather than transactions. Internally, the AR states that if Info Edge is unable to transform existing services by leveraging AI, or if its AI and big data capabilities fail to yield satisfactory results, its platforms may not effectively match users, recommend services or scale new AI-first offerings, potentially affecting win rates, market share, revenue and profits; more broadly innovation could render existing propositions redundant.
risks.risk: AI disintermediation of search-led discovery, and failure to transform existing services with AI

risks.note: The Company stores and processes large volumes of personal and behavioural data and faces technical failures, server breakdowns, data corruption, security breaches and improper use or disclosure of personal information; any such event could deter users, damage reputation, create legal liability, invite regulatory scrutiny and materially affect the business. The BRSR names Cybersecurity and Data Privacy as material issue #1 and specifies regulatory penalties under India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 as a negative financial implication. Mitigations stated: a secondary disaster recovery site in India, continuous AI/ML-driven security monitoring, data encryption, network protection, internal and third-party assessment, industry-standards compliance and proactive management of technology obsolescence.

The AR states the Company carries a large exposure to investee startups spanning listed, non-listed and strategic investments, that these may not generate returns and could absorb additional cash during incubation or early stages, and that a substantial part of investments made over the years has already been written off, exited or provisioned for - described as calculated risks forming part of the growth strategy. Critically, it also warns that reported equity holdings in investee companies may not translate into an equivalent economic interest, due to the terms of investment (including senior rights granted to certain investors) or ESOP-related dilution. Exposure and write-off amounts are financial-statement data and are deliberately not extracted here.
risks.risk: Investment portfolio risk (startup and AIF exposure)

risks.note: All of the Company's platforms face direct competition in both online and offline spaces. Managed through continuous competitive tracking, product innovation, brand investment and customer engagement. This sits alongside 'Brand Value' risk - the platforms are built on well-known brands, and any negative implication for those brands, amplified by the reach of social media, is called a significant risk.

Most of the portfolio depends on network effects - platform value rises with user count - so declining participation, quality erosion or platform disintermediation is a direct business risk. Separately, users may engage in intentional or negligent misconduct including fraudulent postings, spam or inappropriate content, which may damage brand image or expose the Company to claims such as defamation or invasion of privacy; continuous web-traffic monitoring, content filters and profile verification are the stated controls.
risks.risk: Network effects, platform integrity and user-generated content liability

risks.note: The Company operates where government continues to consider regulation of various facets of online businesses, with many such regulations at different levels of deliberation that could significantly impact product offerings and services. Changes in privacy laws may impact its ability to collect, process or share personal data; it typically seeks users' prior consent before sharing, but the evolving legal landscape requires continuing attention (the sentence is truncated in the source).

Revenues from certain segments are sensitive to the economic cycle, with trade wars, tariff barriers, geopolitical conflict, persistent inflation and tighter financial conditions named; business diversification and a healthy balance sheet are the stated mitigants. Related treasury risk: the Company holds significant cash and cash equivalents to preserve financial flexibility, and channels part of it into treasury investments to earn returns, exposing it to market conditions and interest-rate movements - managed through prudent balance-sheet management and a defined investment framework. A third channel is capital availability: given the current phase of the expansion strategy, the Company may need additional capital and could face challenges obtaining it in a timely manner or on acceptable terms.
